\section{The finitary Shannon calculus}

Throughout, $\Omega$ is a finite nonempty set of $N$ points, each of weight $1/N$. Logarithms are natural; divide by $\log 2$ to obtain bits.

\begin{definition}[Statistic, entropy]
A \emph{statistic} is a function $f:\Omega\to A$. Its count function is $c_f(a)=|\{x\in\Omega: f(x)=a\}|$ and its image $\im f$ is the set of $a$ with $c_f(a)>0$. Its entropy is
\[
H(f)=-\sum_{a\in\im f}\frac{c_f(a)}{N}\log\frac{c_f(a)}{N},\qquad H_2(f)=H(f)/\log 2 .
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Pairing, information, residual entropy]
For $f:\Omega\to A$, $g:\Omega\to B$ the pair $(f,g)$ is $x\mapsto(f(x),g(x))$. For a \emph{label} $L:\Omega\to\Lambda$,
\[
I(L;f)=H(L)+H(f)-H(L,f),\qquad H(f\mid L)=H(f,L)-H(L).
\]
\end{definition}

We use the following standard finite facts:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(E1)] $0\le H(f)\le\log|\im f|$.
\item[(E2)] $H(\varphi\circ f)=H(f)$ for injective $\varphi$; in particular $H(f,g)=H(g,f)$.
\item[(E3)] (Subadditivity) $H(f,g)\le H(f)+H(g)$.
\item[(M1)] $0\le I(L;f)\le\min(H(L),H(f))$.
\item[(M2)] (Data processing) $I(L;\varphi\circ f)\le I(L;f)$ for every function $\varphi$.
\item[(M3)] $I(L;(f,g))\le I(L;f)+H(g)$.
\item[(M4)] If $f$ determines $L$, then $I(L;f)=H(L)$.
\end{itemize}
(M3) is the chain-rule estimate $I(L;f,g)-I(L;f)=H(g\mid f)-H(g\mid L,f)\le H(g)$.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:subsingleton}
If $f$ takes values in a set with at most one element, then $H(f)=0$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
By (E1), $0\le H(f)\le\log 1=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Information--residual split]\label{lem:split}
$H(f)=I(L;f)+H(f\mid L)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
$I(L;f)+H(f\mid L)=H(L)+H(f)-H(L,f)+H(f,L)-H(L)=H(f)$ by (E2).
\end{proof}

\section{Batteries and capacity}

\begin{definition}[Battery, capacity]
A \emph{battery} is a family $F=(F_i)_{i\in\iota}$ of statistics $F_i:\Omega\to A$. For finite $S\subseteq\iota$ the reading $F|_S:\Omega\to A^S$ is $x\mapsto(F_i(x))_{i\in S}$, and the \emph{capacity} of $S$ is $\cp(S)=I(L;F|_S)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Basic properties]\label{thm:basic}
For every label $L$ and battery $F$:
(1) $\cp(S)\ge0$; (2) $\cp(S)\le H(L)$; (3) $\cp(\varnothing)=0$; (4) $S\subseteq T\Rightarrow\cp(S)\le\cp(T)$; (5) $\cp(\{i\})=I(L;F_i)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
(1), (2) are (M1). (3): $A^\varnothing$ is a singleton, so $0\le\cp(\varnothing)\le H(F|_\varnothing)=0$ by (M1) and Lemma~\ref{lem:subsingleton}. (4): $F|_S=\pi\circ F|_T$ for the coordinate projection $\pi$; apply (M2). (5): $F|_{\{i\}}$ and $F_i$ are functions of one another; apply (M2) twice.
\end{proof}

\section{The incremental capacity law}

\begin{lemma}[One dial]\label{lem:onedial}
$\cp(S\cup\{j\})\le\cp(S)+H(F_j)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Let $u:A^S\times A\to A^{S\cup\{j\}}$ put $v_i$ in coordinate $i\in S$ and $a$ in the remaining coordinate $j$. Then $F|_{S\cup\{j\}}=u\circ(F|_S,F_j)$, and by (M2), (M3),
$\cp(S\cup\{j\})\le I(L;(F|_S,F_j))\le\cp(S)+H(F_j)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Incremental capacity law]\label{thm:incr}
For all finite $S,T\subseteq\iota$: $\ \cp(S\cup T)\le\cp(S)+\sum_{i\in T}H(F_i)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Induction on $T$: the case $T=\varnothing$ is trivial, and adding $j\notin T$ costs at most $H(F_j)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:onedial} applied to $S\cup T$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:sumH}
$\cp(T)\le\sum_{i\in T}H(F_i)$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Take $S=\varnothing$ and use $\cp(\varnothing)=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Capacity-lattice consistency]\label{thm:lattice}
For finite $S\subseteq T$,
\[
0\le\cp(S)\le\cp(T)\le\min\Bigl(H(L),\ \cp(S)+\sum_{i\in T\setminus S}H(F_i)\Bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:basic} (1), (4), (2), and Theorem~\ref{thm:incr} with $S\cup(T\setminus S)=T$.
\end{proof}

\section{Synergy as interaction information}

\begin{definition}
For a label $L$ and dials $f,g$:
\begin{align*}
\Syn(f,g)&=I(L;(f,g))-I(L;f)-I(L;g),\\
I(f;g)&=H(f)+H(g)-H(f,g),\\
I(f;g\mid L)&=H(L,f)+H(L,g)-H(L,(f,g))-H(L).
\end{align*}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Synergy equals interaction information]\label{thm:interaction}
$\Syn(f,g)=I(f;g\mid L)-I(f;g)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Expanding every mutual information by definition,
$\Syn=[H(L)+H(f,g)-H(L,(f,g))]-[H(L)+H(f)-H(L,f)]-[H(L)+H(g)-H(L,g)]$, and regrouping gives $I(f;g\mid L)-I(f;g)$.
\end{proof}

\section{The synergy sandwich and its sharpness}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:pair}
$I(L;(f,g))=I(L;(g,f))$ and $\max(I(L;f),I(L;g))\le I(L;(f,g))$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Swap and projection maps with (M2).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Synergy sandwich]\label{thm:sandwich}
\[
-\min\bigl(I(L;f),I(L;g)\bigr)\le\Syn(f,g)\le\min\bigl(H(f\mid L),H(g\mid L)\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Lower bound: by Lemma~\ref{lem:pair}, $I(L;(f,g))\ge I(L;f)$ gives $\Syn\ge-I(L;g)$, and symmetrically $\Syn\ge-I(L;f)$. Upper bound: by (M3), $I(L;(f,g))\le I(L;f)+H(g)$, so $\Syn\le H(g)-I(L;g)=H(g\mid L)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:split}; exchanging roles via Lemma~\ref{lem:pair} gives $\Syn\le H(f\mid L)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Sharpness: the XOR battery]\label{thm:xor}
Let $\Omega=\{0,1\}^2$, $L=x_1\oplus x_2$, $f=x_1$, $g=x_2$. Then $I(L;f)=I(L;g)=0$, $I(L;(f,g))=\log2$, and
$\Syn(f,g)=\log2=\min(H(f\mid L),H(g\mid L))$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$L,f,g$ each take each value on two of four points, so each has entropy $\log4-\log2=\log2$. The pairs $(L,f)$, $(L,g)$ are injective, so have entropy $\log 4=2\log2$; hence $I(L;f)=I(L;g)=0$. $(f,g)$ is injective, so determines $L$, and (M4) gives $I(L;(f,g))=\log2$. Thus $\Syn=\log2$, and $H(f\mid L)=H(g\mid L)=2\log2-\log2=\log2$.
\end{proof}

\section{The entropy-column obstruction and the audit}

\begin{theorem}[Entropy-column obstruction]\label{thm:obstruction}
If $H_2(f)=a$, $H_2(g)=b$, $H_2(f,g)=c$, then $c\le a+b$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Divide (E3) by $\log 2>0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:notentropy}
No statistics $f,g$ on any finite sample satisfy $H_2(f)=H_2(g)=1.0012$ and $H_2(f,g)=2.1314$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Otherwise $2.1314\le2.0024$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The recorded $S_3$a $\times$ $S_3$b row is therefore impossible as an entropy triple, but admissible as an information triple: Theorem~\ref{thm:sandwich} only demands joint $\ge$ max of marginals from below, and the positive synergy $2.1314-2.0024=0.1290$ bits must be funded by the residual entropies. The $A_4\times D_4$ row is likewise super-additive, $1.9125>0.4733+1.4342=1.9075$, so it cannot be an entropy triple either.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[The recorded table passes the necessary checks]
In bits: (1) $1.0012\le2.1314$, $0.4733\le1.9125$, $1.4342\le1.9125$; (2) $2.1314\le8.2246$, $1.9125\le8.2246$; (3) $8.2246\le9.5276$, the label-entropy ceiling used in the audit; (4) $2.1314-2\cdot1.0012=+0.1290\ge-1.0012$ and $1.9125-0.4733-1.4342=+0.0050\ge-0.4733$; (5) all spreads are at most $0.0040$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Arithmetic. Items (1)--(2) instantiate Theorem~\ref{thm:basic}(4), (3) Theorem~\ref{thm:basic}(2), and (4) Theorem~\ref{thm:sandwich}.
\end{proof}

The overlap row is not constrained by any law of this paper.

\section{The battery synergy budget}

\begin{theorem}[Battery synergy budget]\label{thm:budget}
For finite $T$: $\ \cp(T)-\sum_{i\in T}I(L;F_i)\le\sum_{i\in T}H(F_i\mid L)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:split} and Theorem~\ref{thm:basic}(5), $\sum_iH(F_i)=\sum_i\cp(\{i\})+\sum_iH(F_i\mid L)$; combine with Corollary~\ref{cor:sumH}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Forced residual entropy]\label{cor:forced}
If $\cp(T)=8.2246$ bits and $\sum_{i\in T}I(L;F_i)=3.9099$ bits, then $\sum_{i\in T}H(F_i\mid L)\ge4.3147$ bits.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Divide Theorem~\ref{thm:budget} by $\log2$; $8.2246-3.9099=4.3147$.
\end{proof}

This is a falsifiable prediction about a quantity not yet recorded.

\section{Capacity is not submodular}

A set function $\phi$ is \emph{submodular} if $\phi(S\cup\{i,j\})-\phi(S\cup\{i\})-\phi(S\cup\{j\})+\phi(S)\le0$ whenever $i,j\notin S$; monotone submodular functions are the setting of the classical $(1-1/e)$ greedy guarantee.

\begin{theorem}[Capacity is monotone but not submodular]\label{thm:nonsub}
For the XOR battery ($\Omega=\{0,1\}^2$, $L=x_1\oplus x_2$, $F_1=x_1$, $F_2=x_2$),
\[
\cp(\{1,2\})-\cp(\{1\})-\cp(\{2\})+\cp(\varnothing)=\log2>0.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\cp(\{1\})=\cp(\{2\})=0$ by Theorems~\ref{thm:basic}(5) and~\ref{thm:xor}; $F|_{\{1,2\}}$ is injective, so $\cp(\{1,2\})=H(L)=\log2$ by (M4); and $\cp(\varnothing)=0$.
\end{proof}

\section{An arithmetic example}

Let $f(p)$, $g(p)$ be the numbers of roots modulo $p$ of $x^3-x-1$ (discriminant $-23$) and $x^3+x+1$ (discriminant $-31$), and $L(p)=\bigl(\tfrac{-23}{p}\bigr)\bigl(\tfrac{-31}{p}\bigr)$. \section{Algorithms}

\textbf{A (empirical capacity).} Form the tuple column $F|_S$, count multiplicities of $L$, $F|_S$ and $(L,F|_S)$ by hashing, and return $H(L)+H(F|_S)-H(L,F|_S)$; cost $O(N|S|)$, and $O(2^kNk)$ for the whole lattice of $k$ dials.

\textbf{C (submodularity test).} Evaluate all second differences $\Delta_{ij}(S)$ from the memoised lattice and report positive values; $O(k^22^k)$ lookups.

With these laws, ``all checks pass'' certifies joint consistency of the recorded values with monotonicity, the label ceiling, the synergy lower bound and the recording tolerance, and identifies the joint column as informations. from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import math
import random
from collections import Counter
from typing import Callable, Hashable, Sequence

LOG2: float = math.log(2.0)
Sample = Sequence[Hashable]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Empirical Shannon calculus on a finite, uniformly weighted sample
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def entropy(values: Sample) -> float:
    """Plug-in entropy (nats) of a statistic observed on a uniform finite sample."""
    n = len(values)
    return -sum((c / n) * math.log(c / n) for c in Counter(values).values())


def bits(x: float) -> float:
    return x / LOG2


def pair(f: Sample, g: Sample) -> list[tuple[Hashable, Hashable]]:
    return list(zip(f, g))


def mutual_info(label: Sample, f: Sample) -> float:
    """I(L;f) = H(L) + H(f) - H(L,f)."""
    return entropy(label) + entropy(f) - entropy(pair(label, f))


def cond_entropy(f: Sample, label: Sample) -> float:
    """Residual entropy H(f|L) = H(f,L) - H(L)."""
    return entropy(pair(f, label)) - entropy(label)


def sub_battery(battery: Sequence[Sample], subset: Sequence[int]) -> list[tuple]:
    """Joint reading of the dials with indices in `subset`."""
    n = len(battery[0]) if battery else 0
    return [tuple(battery[i][x] for i in sorted(subset)) for x in range(n)]


def capacity(label: Sample, battery: Sequence[Sample], subset: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """cap(S) = I(L ; F|_S); the empty battery reads a constant."""

A research programme has written the same information values — in **bits** — into its ledger again and again across twenty-seven studies. An audit of eight of them found **zero inconsistencies** (maximal spread $0.0040$ bits). This page asks the question an audit alone cannot answer: *are the recorded numbers even possible?* We will build, step by step, the laws that every honest table of information values must obey, and then turn them loose on the real table.

## 1. The ledger

| quantity | recordings (bits) | spread |
|---|---|---|
| $S_3$a marginal | $1.0012$, $1.0012$ | $0.0000$ |
| $S_3$b marginal | $1.0008$, $1.0012$ | $0.0004$ |
| $A_4$ marginal | $0.4733$, $0.4733$ | $0.0000$ |
| $D_4$ marginal | $1.4302$, $1.4342$ | $0.0040$ |
| $S_3$a $\times$ $S_3$b joint | $2.1314$, $2.1314$ | $0.0000$ |
| $A_4\times D_4$ joint | $1.9125$, $1.9125$ | $0.0000$ |
| $S_3$a $\times$ $S_3$b overlap | $0.9919$, $0.9919$ | $0.0000$ |
| four-field battery capacity | $8.2246$, $8.2246$ | $0.0000$ |

The sample points are primes; each **dial** records how a prime splits in a fixed number field (Galois groups $S_3$, $A_4$, $D_4$); each number is how much a dial, a pair of dials, or a four-dial **battery** tells us about a fixed **label**.

<details><summary>Background: entropy and mutual information on a finite sample</summary>

On a finite sample $\Omega$ of $N$ equally weighted points, a statistic $f$ has entropy $H(f) = -\sum_a \frac{c_a}{N}\log\frac{c_a}{N}$, where $c_a$ counts the points with $f = a$. The mutual information with a label is $I(L;f) = H(L) + H(f) - H(L,f)$ and the residual entropy is $H(f\mid L) = H(f,L) - H(L)$. Divide by $\log 2$ for bits. See [Entropy (information theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entropy_(information_theory)) and [Mutual information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutual_information).
</details>

{{visualization:1}}

## 2. Law one — the capacity lattice

For a sub-battery $S$, the **capacity** is $\mathrm{cap}(S) = I(L; F|_S)$: what the dials in $S$, read together, reveal about the label. Three facts hold for *every* sample:

- **Monotone:** $S\subseteq T \Rightarrow \mathrm{cap}(S)\le\mathrm{cap}(T)$ (forgetting dials is post-processing, and post-processing loses information).
- **Floor and ceiling:** $\mathrm{cap}(\varnothing)=0$ and $\mathrm{cap}(S)\le H(L)$.
- **Incremental law:** $\mathrm{cap}(S\cup T)\le \mathrm{cap}(S)+\sum_{i\in T}H(F_i)$ — a dial cannot carry more news than it has room for.

Together: for $S\subseteq T$,
$$0 \le \mathrm{cap}(S) \le \mathrm{cap}(T) \le \min\Big(H(L),\ \mathrm{cap}(S)+\sum_{i\in T\setminus S}H(F_i)\Big).$$

<details><summary>Proof sketch of the incremental law</summary>

For one dial: the reading of $S\cup\{j\}$ is a function of the pair $(F|_S, F_j)$, so by data processing $\mathrm{cap}(S\cup\{j\}) \le I(L;F|_S,F_j)$. The chain rule gives $I(L;X,Y) - I(L;X) = H(Y\mid X) - H(Y\mid L,X) \le H(Y)$. So adding dial $j$ costs at most $H(F_j)$. Induct on $T$ one dial at a time. Starting from $S=\varnothing$ gives $\mathrm{cap}(T)\le\sum_{i\in T}H(F_i)$.
</details>

{{algorithm:0}}

{{visualization:2}}

Notice something odd in that lattice: dials $1$ and $2$ are worth nothing alone, yet together they are worth a full bit. Keep that in mind.

## 3. Law two — synergy and its sandwich

The $S_3$ pair carries $2.1314$ bits, but its members carry only $1.0012$ each. The surplus is the **synergy**
$$\mathrm{Syn}(f,g) = I(L;f,g) - I(L;f) - I(L;g) = 2.1314 - 2.0024 = 0.1290 \text{ bits}.$$

Two theorems pin it down:

- **Interaction identity:** $\mathrm{Syn}(f,g) = I(f;g\mid L) - I(f;g)$ — conditional coupling minus redundancy ([interaction information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interaction_information)).
- **Synergy sandwich:** $-\min(I(L;f),I(L;g)) \le \mathrm{Syn}(f,g) \le \min(H(f\mid L),H(g\mid L))$.

The upper wall says synergy must be *paid for* out of residual entropy. Try to break the sandwich yourself:

{{interactive_demo:0}}

<details><summary>Proof sketch of the sandwich</summary>

*Lower:* the pair knows at least as much as either member, so $I(L;f,g)\ge I(L;f)$, i.e. $\mathrm{Syn}\ge -I(L;g)$; symmetrically $\mathrm{Syn}\ge -I(L;f)$.
*Upper:* $I(L;f,g)\le I(L;f)+H(g)$ gives $\mathrm{Syn}\le H(g)-I(L;g)=H(g\mid L)$, using $H(g)=I(L;g)+H(g\mid L)$; swap roles for $H(f\mid L)$.
</details>

### The XOR battery: the sandwich is sharp

Flip two fair coins, label $L=x_1\oplus x_2$, dials $x_1$ and $x_2$. Each dial alone: $0$ bits. Both: $1$ bit. Synergy $= 1$ bit $= H(x_1\mid L) = H(x_2\mid L)$. This is [secret sharing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_sharing) in miniature, and it shows the upper bound cannot be improved.

{{visualization:0}}

### Capacity is not submodular

Diminishing returns ([submodularity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submodular_set_function)) is what makes greedy feature selection provably good. For XOR,
$$\mathrm{cap}(\{1,2\}) - \mathrm{cap}(\{1\}) - \mathrm{cap}(\{2\}) + \mathrm{cap}(\varnothing) = \log 2 > 0.$$
Capacity is monotone but **not** submodular: complements, not substitutes.

{{algorithm:2}}

## 4. The critic's catch

Entropies obey **subadditivity**: $H(f,g)\le H(f)+H(g)$. So a marginal/marginal/joint triple of *entropies* must satisfy joint $\le$ sum. The $S_3$ row has $2.1314 > 2.0024$. **No pair of statistics on any finite sample has these entropies.** The row is self-consistent recording-to-recording, yet impossible as entropies — it can only be a row of *informations about the label*, where the synergy sandwich permits the surplus. (The $A_4\times D_4$ row is also super-additive: $1.9125 > 1.9075$.)

## 5. A prediction: the battery synergy budget

Summing the ideas over a whole battery:
$$\mathrm{cap}(T) - \sum_{i\in T} I(L;F_i) \le \sum_{i\in T} H(F_i\mid L).$$
With capacity $8.2246$ bits and marginals summing to $3.9099$ bits, the four dials' residual entropies are **forced** to total at least $4.3147$ bits — a quantity nobody has recorded yet. Measure it; if it comes up short, the ledger is wrong somewhere.

<details><summary>Proof sketch</summary>

Each dial splits as $H(F_i) = I(L;F_i) + H(F_i\mid L)$, and $\mathrm{cap}(T)\le\sum_i H(F_i)$ by the incremental law. Subtract.
</details>

## 6. XOR in the primes

The phenomenon is not a toy. Count roots mod $p$ of $x^3-x-1$ (discriminant $-23$) and $x^3+x+1$ (discriminant $-31$), and take the label $\left(\frac{-23}{p}\right)\left(\frac{-31}{p}\right)$. Each root count fixes the parity of its own Frobenius permutation, hence its own Legendre symbol — but not the other's. import Mathlib
import Combinatorics.TraceBatteryEntropy
import MachineLearning.BatterySynergy.MutualInformation

namespace CrossProgrammeConsistency

open TraceBattery BatterySynergy Finset

variable {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] {Λ α β : Type*} {ι : Type*}

/-! ## 1. Sub-batteries and their capacity -/

/-- The joint reading of the dials in `S` of the battery `F`. -/
def sub (F : ι → Ω → α) (S : Finset ι) : Ω → (S → α) := fun x i => F i x

/-- The trace capacity (in nats) of the sub-battery `S` against the label `L`. -/
noncomputable def cap (L : Ω → Λ) (F : ι → Ω → α) (S : Finset ι) : ℝ := MI L (sub F S)

/-- **Monotonicity.**  A larger battery never carries less information. -/
theorem cap_mono (L : Ω → Λ) (F : ι → Ω → α) {S T : Finset ι} (hST : S ⊆ T) :
    cap L F S ≤ cap L F T := by
  have h : sub F S = (fun (v : T → α) (i : S) => v ⟨i, hST i.2⟩) ∘ sub F T := rfl
  unfold cap
  rw [h]
  exact MI_comp_le L (sub F T) _

/-- The capacity is capped by the label entropy. -/
theorem cap_le_label (L : Ω → Λ) (F : ι → Ω → α) (S : Finset ι) :
    cap L F S ≤ H L := MI_le_label_entropy L _

/-- The capacity is nonnegative. -/
theorem cap_nonneg (L : Ω → Λ) (F : ι → Ω → α) (S : Finset ι) :
    0 ≤ cap L F S := MI_nonneg L _

/-- A statistic with values in a subsingleton type has zero entropy. -/
theorem H_eq_zero_of_subsingleton {γ : Type*} [Subsingleton γ] (f : Ω → γ) : H f = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (H_nonneg f)
  have hcard : (img f).card ≤ 1 := Finset.card_le_one.2 fun a _ b _ => Subsingleton.elim a b
  have hle := H_le_log_card_img f
  interval_cases h : (img f).card
  · simpa using hle
  · simpa using hle

/-- The empty battery carries no information. -/
theorem cap_empty (L : Ω → Λ) (F : ι → Ω → α) : cap L F ∅ = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (cap_nonneg L F ∅)
  have : Subsingleton ((∅ : Finset ι) → α) :=
    ⟨fun u v => funext fun i => absurd i.2 (Finset.notMem_empty _)⟩
  calc cap L F ∅ ≤ H (sub F ∅) := MI_le_stat_entropy L _
    _ = 0 := H_eq_zero_of_subsingleton _

/-! ## 2. The incremental capacity law -/

/-- **Adding one dial** raises the capacity by at most that dial's entropy. -/
theorem cap_insert_le [DecidableEq ι] (L : Ω → Λ) (F : ι → Ω → α) (S : Finset ι) (j : ι) :
    cap L F (insert j S) ≤ cap L F S + H (F j) := by
  classical
  let u : (S → α) × α → (↥(insert j S) → α) :=
    fun p i => if h : (i : ι) ∈ S then p.1 ⟨i, h⟩ else p.2
  have hu : sub F (insert j S) = u ∘ (fun x => (sub F S x, F j x)) := by
    funext x i
    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := i
    by_cases h : i ∈ S
    · simp [u, sub, h]
    · have : i = j := by
        rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 hi with h' | h'
        · exact h'
        · exact absurd h' h
      subst this
      simp [u, sub, h]
  calc cap L F (insert j S) = MI L (u ∘ (fun x => (sub F S x, F j x))) := by
        rw [cap, hu]
    _ ≤ MI L (fun x => (sub F S x, F j x)) := MI_comp_le L _ u
    _ ≤ MI L (sub F S) + H (F j) := MI_pair_le_add_H L (sub F S) (F j)
    _ = cap L F S + H (F j) := rfl

/-- **Incremental capacity law.**  Adjoining the dials of `T` to a battery `S`
raises its capacity by at most `Σ_{i ∈ T} H(Fᵢ)`. -/
theorem cap_union_le [DecidableEq ι] (L : Ω → Λ) (F : ι → Ω → α) (S T : Finset ι) :
    cap L F (S ∪ T) ≤ cap L F S + ∑ i ∈ T, H (F i) := by
  induction T using Finset.induction_on with
  | empty => simp
  | insert j T hj ih =>
    rw [Finset.union_insert, Finset.sum_insert hj]
    have := cap_insert_le L F (S ∪ T) j
    linarith

/-- The capacity of a battery is at most the sum of its dial entropies. -/
theorem cap_le_sum_H [DecidableEq ι] (L : Ω → Λ) (F : ι → Ω → α) (T : Finset ι) :
    cap L F T ≤ ∑ i ∈ T, H (F i) := by
  have := cap_union_le L F ∅ T
  rw [Finset.empty_union, cap_empty] at this
  linarith

/-- **Capacity-lattice consistency.**  For nested batteries `S ⊆ T` every recording
of their capacities must obey
`0 ≤ cap S ≤ cap T ≤ min (H L) (cap S + Σ_{i ∈ T \ S} H(Fᵢ))`. -/
theorem cap_lattice_consistency [DecidableEq ι] (L : Ω → Λ) (F : ι → Ω → α)
    {S T : Finset ι} (hST : S ⊆ T) :
    0 ≤ cap L F S ∧ cap L F S ≤ cap L F T ∧
      cap L F T ≤ min (H L) (cap L F S + ∑ i ∈ T \ S, H (F i)) := by
  refine ⟨cap_nonneg L F S, cap_mono L F hST, le_min (cap_le_label L F T) ?_⟩
  have h := cap_union_le L F S (T \ S)
  rwa [Finset.union_sdiff_of_subset hST] at h

/-! ## 3. Synergy and interaction information -/

/-- The joint reading of two statistics. -/
def pair (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) : Ω → α × β := fun x => (f x, g x)

/-- Synergy of two dials about a label. -/
noncomputable def Syn (L : Ω → Λ) (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) : ℝ :=
  MI L (pair f g) - MI L f - MI L g

/-- Mutual information between two dials. -/
noncomputable def dialMI (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) : ℝ := H f + H g - H (pair f g)

/-- Conditional mutual information between two dials given the label. -/
noncomputable def condDialMI (L : Ω → Λ) (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) : ℝ :=
  H (pr L f) + H (pr L g) - H (pr L (pair f g)) - H L

/-- **Synergy is interaction information**:
`I(L; f,g) - I(L;f) - I(L;g) = I(f;g | L) - I(f;g)`. -/
theorem synergy_eq_interaction (L : Ω → Λ) (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) :
    Syn L f g = condDialMI L f g - dialMI f g := by
  unfold Syn condDialMI dialMI
  rw [MI_eq, MI_eq, MI_eq]
  ring

/-- `H(pr g L) = H(pr L g)`: the order of the coordinates is irrelevant. -/
theorem H_pr_swap (L : Ω → Λ) (g : Ω → β) : H (pr g L) = H (pr L g) := by
  have h : pr g L = Prod.swap ∘ pr L g := rfl
  rw [h, H_comp_eq_of_injective _ Prod.swap_injective]

/-- The two orders of a pair carry the same information. -/
theorem MI_pair_comm (L : Ω → Λ) (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) :
    MI L (pair f g) = MI L (pair g f) := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · have h : pair f g = Prod.swap ∘ pair g f := rfl
    rw [h]; exact MI_comp_le L _ _
  · have h : pair g f = Prod.swap ∘ pair f g := rfl
    rw [h]; exact MI_comp_le L _ _

/-- The pair carries at least as much as either component. -/
theorem MI_le_pair_left (L : Ω → Λ) (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) : MI L f ≤ MI L (pair f g) := by
  have h : f = Prod.fst ∘ pair f g := rfl
  conv_lhs => rw [h]
  exact MI_comp_le L _ _

theorem MI_le_pair_right (L : Ω → Λ) (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) : MI L g ≤ MI L (pair f g) := by
  have h : g = Prod.snd ∘ pair f g := rfl
  conv_lhs => rw [h]

def primes_up_to(n: int) -> list[int]:
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for p in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p * p::p] = bytearray(len(sieve[p * p::p]))
    return [p for p in range(n + 1) if sieve[p]]


def root_count(poly: Callable[[int], int], p: int) -> int:
    """Number of roots of a cubic modulo p: 3 (split), 1 (linear x quadratic), 0 (inert)."""
    return sum(1 for x in range(p) if poly(x) % p == 0)


def legendre(a: int, p: int) -> int:
    r = pow(a % p, (p - 1) // 2, p)
    return -1 if r == p - 1 else r


def arithmetic_xor(limit: int = 4000) -> None:
    """Dials: number of roots of x^3-x-1 (disc -23) and x^3+x+1 (disc -31) mod p.
    Label: (-23/p)(-31/p), the product of the signs of the two Frobenius permutations.
    Each type alone determines only its own sign, so it says (almost) nothing about the
    product; together they determine it -- a naturally occurring XOR battery."""
    ps = [p for p in primes_up_to(limit) if p not in (2, 3, 23, 31)]
    f = [root_count(lambda x: x ** 3 - x - 1, p) for p in ps]
    g = [root_count(lambda x: x ** 3 + x + 1, p) for p in ps]
    L = [legendre(-23, p) * legendre(-31, p) for p in ps]

          f"I(L;f,g) = {bits(mutual_info(L, pair(f, g))):.4f} bits")
    syn = synergy(L, f, g)
    hi = min(cond_entropy(f, L), cond_entropy(g, L))
    print(f"    Syn = {bits(syn):.4f} bits <= min(H(f|L),H(g|L)) = {bits(hi):.4f} bits")
    print(f"    redundancy I(f;g) = {bits(dial_mi(f, g)):.4f}, conditional I(f;g|L) = "
          f"{bits(cond_dial_mi(L, f, g)):.4f}  (Syn = difference)")
    d2 = capacity(L, F, [0, 1]) - capacity(L, F, [0]) - capacity(L, F, [1]) + capacity(L, F, [])
    print(f"    second difference of capacity = {bits(d2):.4f} bits > 0 (non-submodular in the wild)")
